The rule on getting back contested cards is: if all but one copy of the
card is yielded, the "controller" of the last copy gets control of it
again during his or her next untap phase, unless of course it becomes
contested again in the meantime. Nice and simple, with no band-aid
to hold the hand of someone who contests their own card.

--

Subject: Re: Q: Self Contest -- Tom?
From: aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie)

Message-Id: <4q6tj0$n...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>
Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-Cards.jyhad

page 37, Vampire rulebook:
"If a previously contested card ceases to be contested, you return the card
to the active region, face up and untapped, during your next untap phase."

Note "at the end of an untap phase", but during one. No exception for
the card being yielded during your untap phase. If a card stops being
contested, you *must* wait until your *next* untap phase; if you're currently
in your untap phase, that means the untap phase of your next turn.

No. Since neither Duck will be "won" during this untap phase, you
have to pay to contest or yield each copy. You can order this in
any way you want:

1) Pay to contest a copy
2) Yield the other copy

or

1) Yield a copy
2) Pay to contest the other copy

or

1) Yield a copy
2) Yield the other copy

or

1) Pay to contest a copy
2) Pay to contest the other copy

(I wouldn't recommend this last alternative :-)



Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
JlB1925 (jlb...@aol.com) wrote:
: >There is a general rule that you can order untap events, no? Or do I

: have
: >this mixed up with something else.
: I believe there are no Magic Timing Games in V:TES. Everything that
: happens in one phase happens at once (except master/minion phase actions).
: So, no gaining from the edge then burning it to remove a threat counter.

There is no MtG timing, true. So everything happens in sequence (not
all at once, nor in a Last-in-first-out stack, etc.)

The first thing that happens during your untap is that all of your
cards must be untapped. Any other untap events may be applying in
whatever order you choose.

From the rulebook:

6.1 The Untap Phase

Some cards in play may cause some or all players to perform actions during
your untap phase. Any cards requiring you to take an action or actions
during your untap phase take effect after you've untapped your cards. If
more than one card requires you to take an action, you may choose the order
in which these actions take place.

--

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Steve Wampler ("sek10"@cornellSHA.edu) wrote:
: L. Scott Johnson wrote:
: > The first thing that happens during your untap is that all of your

: > cards must be untapped. Any other untap events may be applying in
: > whatever order you choose.

: So, CAN you yield one of your copies of a self-contesed card and

: get the other copy that turn without having to pay a pool (and/or wait
: a turn)?

No.

The key to this is in the VtES rules, section 15.

If a previously contested card ceases to be contested, you return
the card to the active region, face up and untapped, during your next untap
phase.

So, you may order the yielding and the contesting (paying one pool)
any way you like, but (in the proposed case) yielding a copy first
will not resolve the problem, since once the last copy is yielded
(during your untap phase), you don't return the other copy to
the active region until your *next* untap. So, during the current
untap phase, you will still have to choose to yield or pay a
pool for the second copy as well.



As per the rulebook, you only get control of a contested card if all other
copies have been yielded by the start of your turn. Nothing you do during
your turn can change the fact that the card is contested at the start of
your turn, so you can't gain control of it until the following turn
(presuming you yield the duplicate copies during this turn's untap).
